entries.question: Shall the measure repealing Redwood City Municipal Code Chapter 42 and replacing it with a new Chapter 42 that (1) limits rent increases on multifamily housing built before February 1, 1995; (2) expands just-cause eviction protections to most rental housing, including single-family homes, ADUs, and affordable housing; (3) requires new City administration estimated to cost $5 million to $11 million annually, funded by annual rental property owner fees; and (4) increases relocation assistance for no-fault evictions, be adopted?
entries.explanation: Replace Redwood City’s rental-housing rules with expanded rent limits, eviction protections and relocation assistance. For covered units built before February 1, 1995, annual rent increases would generally be limited to 60% of local inflation, capped at 5%, with petitions for adjustments in specified circumstances. The question estimates $5 million to $11 million in annual city administration costs, funded by rental-property owner fees.

notes: Rent limits and eviction protections cover different groups of properties. The city attorney’s analysis describes the coverage, exceptions, rent-adjustment petitions and relocation payments.

entries.question: Shall the measure amending the City of San Mateo’s Charter to reflect the City’s current district-based election system, update the process for scheduling Council meetings and filling Council vacancies, update or remove obsolete provisions, and make other technical and conforming changes, be adopted?
